prerequisites: Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical-mathematical description of particle motion and know the magnitudes that quantify it.
Understand the laws and theorems that relate particle motion to the causes that provoke it.
Understand the concepts and principles necessary for the study of heat exchange processes in closed systems of ideal gases.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Physical quantities. Treatment of measurement errors.
Thermometry and calorimetry. First law of thermodynamics.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade (NFO) is calculated as NFO = EvC + (1 – EvC/10) × CGO, where EvC is the continuous assessment grade and CGO is the global exam grade. This formula applies only if CGO is 3.5 points or higher out of 10. A minimum global score of 2.0 points out of 5.5 is required for continuous assessment; otherwise, continuous assessment is zero. If the continuous assessment is lost or chosen not to be taken, the final grade is equal to the global exam grade (NFE = CGE). Any final score below 5.0 points will result in a FAIL. For extraordinary calls, the continuous assessment grade (EvC) from the ordinary period is retained and combined with the extraordinary global exam (CGE) using the same formula, provided CGE is 3.5 points or higher. If not, the final grade is equal to CGE. Any final score below 5.0 points will result in a FAIL. Academic integrity violations will result in a 0-FAIL grade.
